question:
A 61-year-old male presents with a 10 kg (22 lb) unintentional weight gain over the past 3 months,
along with decreased libido, oily skin, and trouble sleeping. He denies any significant personal or family
medical history but has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 10 years. On examination, he appears
lethargic, with a temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse of 68/min, and blood pressure of 149/88 mm Hg.
Findings include central obesity, acne, thin and easily bruisable skin with abdominal stretch marks,

hyperpigmentation of mucous membranes and skin creases, and proximal muscle weakness and
atrophy. His serum glucose level is 240 mg/dL. Which imaging finding is most likely in this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) Adrenal adenoma (B) Bilateral adrenal hyperplasia (C) Pituitary adenoma (D)
Pulmonary tumor (E) Ectopic ACTH-producing tumor (F) Paraneoplastic syndrome-induced adrenal
hypertrophy (G) Retroperitoneal mass (H) Hypothalamic tumor (I) Adrenal cortical carcinoma (J)
Adrenal hemorrhage
 A. Pituitary adenoma
B. Adrenal hemorrhage
C. Paraneoplastic syndrome-induced adrenal hypertrophy
D. Retroperitoneal mass
E. Ectopic ACTH-producing tumor
F. Adrenal adenoma
G. Bilateral adrenal hyperplasia
H. Adrenal cortical carcinoma
I. Hypothalamic tumor
J. Pulmonary tumor
